## Four layers, four distinct jobs

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "The logical layers of the publishing workflow."
flowchart TB
    subgraph SOURCE["Authoring"]
      Q["Quarto .qmd articles"] 
      M["ci-packages metadata"]
      F["Saved execution results"]
    end
    subgraph NIX["Build tools · Nix"]
      N["Quarto CLI + Pixi CLI + Python utilities"]
    end
    subgraph PIXI["Scientific runtime · Pixi"]
      R["Shared R + Python packages"]
    end
    subgraph WEB["Static website"]
      H["_site HTML + assets"]
      P["gh-pages / GitHub Pages"]
    end
    Q --> N
    M --> N
    F --> N
    N --> R
    R --> H
    H --> P
```

:::: {.docs-card-grid}
::: {.docs-card}
### Nix: Toolchain

`flake.nix` and `flake.lock` define the tools available for rendering and CI validation.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Pixi: Runtime

One `pixi exec` environment combines core dependencies and packages needed by executable articles.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Quarto: Renderer

One project-wide render produces pages, figures, Mermaid diagrams, and browser-ready Observable JS.
:::
::: {.docs-card}
### Pages: Hosting

The rendered `_site` directory is published to the `gh-pages` branch without rerendering.
:::
::::

## What happens when you edit a page?

```{mermaid}
%%| fig-cap: "An edit triggers one whole-site build, not necessarily a rerun of every code chunk."
sequenceDiagram
    actor Author
    participant Main as GitHub main
    participant CI as Actions runner
    participant Q as Quarto
    participant Pages as GitHub Pages
    Author->>Main: Push source change
    Main->>CI: Trigger publish workflow
    CI->>CI: Load Nix tools and run tests
    CI->>CI: Resolve dependencies and freeze matches
    CI->>Q: Render whole site once via Pixi
    Note over CI,Q: Cached code results may be reused
    Q-->>CI: _site HTML and freeze results
    CI->>Pages: Publish pre-rendered HTML
    opt Auto-freeze results changed
      CI->>Main: Commit _freeze + manifest
    end
```

## What exactly is pinned? {.panel-tabset}

### Nix toolchain

[`flake.lock`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/flake.lock) pins the Nixpkgs revision. The resulting Quarto, Pixi and utility tools are selected from that revision.

### Runtime dependencies

`ci-packages` requirements are resolved together with core packages through `pixi exec`. This is convenient but **not** a fully locked Pixi environment: compatible package versions may change over time.

### Research inputs

Source-controlled scripts, relevant data and preserved outputs support reproducibility. External datasets, remote services and cluster computations still require their own provenance and refresh decisions.

:::

The source of truth is [`_quarto.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/_quarto.yml), [`flake.nix`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/flake.nix), [`render-site.py`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/scripts/render-site.py), and [`publish.yml`](https://github.com/YONGHUNI/blog/blob/main/.github/workflows/publish.yml).
